claim: Every AWS account type (standalone, management and member accounts) requires MFA for its root user; a root user without MFA must register a device within 35 days of the first console sign-in attempt. The expansion to member accounts was announced in a post dated Jun 17, 2025, after management accounts in May 2024 and standalone accounts in June 2024.

evidence.quote: All AWS account types (standalone, management, and member accounts) require MFA to be configured for their root user. Users must register MFA within 35 days of their first sign-in attempt to access the AWS Management Console if MFA is not already enabled.

Our security journey began with requiring MFA for AWS Organizations management account root users in May 2024, followed by expanding MFA requirements to standalone account root users in June 2024, and introducing centralized root access management for AWS Organizations in November 2024.
MFA is enforced for all account types for their root user.

evidence.heading: AWS IAM now enforces MFA for root users across all account types

evidence.quote: Today AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) announced comprehensive multi-factor authentication (MFA) requirements for root users across all account types, with the expansion to member accounts.
